sos.what: The driver pressed the emergency (SOS) button and is asking for help.
sos.action: Call the driver right away. If there is no answer, check the live location and send help.

overspeed.what: The vehicle drove faster than the allowed speed.
overspeed.action: Remind the driver of the speed limit. Repeated cases should be reviewed with the driver.

speedOk.what: The vehicle slowed down and is back within the speed limit.
speedOk.action: No action needed — this closes the previous speeding alert.

geofenceEnter.what: The vehicle entered one of the defined areas (geofence).
geofenceEnter.action: Check that the vehicle is supposed to be in this area at this time.

geofenceExit.what: The vehicle left one of the defined areas (geofence).
geofenceExit.action: If the vehicle should stay inside this area, contact the driver.

geofence.what: The vehicle crossed the border of a defined area (geofence).
geofence.action: Open the map to see which area it was and whether that is expected.

offline.what: The tracker stopped sending data, so the vehicle is not visible right now.
offline.action: Usually this is weak mobile coverage or the vehicle being switched off. If it lasts long, check the tracker power and SIM card.

online.what: The tracker is connected again and sending data.

gpsLost.what: The tracker cannot see the satellites, so its location may be wrong or frozen. This often happens in tunnels, covered parking, deep valleys or near tall structures.
gpsLost.action: If it happens in the same place again and again, see the “GPS coverage” map. If it happens everywhere, check the GPS antenna.

gpsBack.what: The tracker sees the satellites again and the location is accurate.

antennaCut.what: The GPS antenna is disconnected or cut, so the location cannot be tracked.
antennaCut.action: This can be tampering. Inspect the antenna and its cable as soon as possible.

jamming.what: Something is blocking the GPS / mobile signal (jamming). This is often deliberate.
jamming.action: Treat it as a possible theft or tampering attempt: contact the driver and watch the vehicle closely.

powerCut.what: The tracker lost its main power from the vehicle and is running on its backup battery.
powerCut.action: Check whether the power cable was disconnected. If nobody did it on purpose, it may be tampering.

powerBack.what: The tracker gets power from the vehicle again.

lowPower.what: The vehicle battery voltage is low.
lowPower.action: Have the vehicle battery and charging system checked so it does not fail to start.

lowBattery.what: The tracker backup battery is almost empty.
lowBattery.action: Make sure the tracker is connected to vehicle power so the battery can recharge.

tow.what: The vehicle moved while the engine was off — it may be towed or carried.
tow.action: If this was not planned, call the driver immediately and follow the vehicle on the map.

crash.what: A strong impact was detected — possibly an accident.
crash.action: Call the driver immediately. If there is no answer, send help to the location.

harshDriving.what: The driver braked, accelerated or turned too sharply.
harshDriving.action: Occasional cases are normal. If it repeats, talk to the driver about safer driving.

fatigue.what: The driver camera saw signs of tiredness (closed eyes, yawning or drowsiness).
fatigue.action: Contact the driver and ask them to stop and rest. Tired driving is very dangerous.

phone.what: The driver camera saw the driver using a phone while driving.
phone.action: Remind the driver that phone use while driving is not allowed.

smoking.what: The driver camera saw the driver smoking.
smoking.action: Remind the driver of the no-smoking rule if it applies to this vehicle.

distraction.what: The driver camera saw that the driver was not looking at the road.
distraction.action: Check the photo or video. If it repeats, talk to the driver.

driverAbsent.what: The driver camera cannot see a driver in the seat, or the driver is not recognized.
driverAbsent.action: Check who is driving the vehicle right now.

cameraBlocked.what: The driver camera is covered or blocked.
cameraBlocked.action: Ask the driver to uncover the camera. Covering it on purpose is a violation.

tooClose.what: The front camera warned that the vehicle got too close to the vehicle or person ahead.
tooClose.action: Remind the driver to keep a safe distance.

laneDeparture.what: The vehicle drifted out of its lane without signaling.
laneDeparture.action: This can be a sign of tiredness or distraction. Check with the driver if it repeats.

blindSpot.what: Something was in the vehicle blind spot while it moved.
blindSpot.action: Check the video if available. No action is needed for a single event.

videoLoss.what: One of the vehicle cameras stopped sending picture.
videoLoss.action: Check the camera cable and connection at the next service.

storage.what: There is a problem with the video recorder memory (full or faulty).
storage.action: Videos may not be saved. Have the memory card checked or replaced.

ignitionOn.action: No action needed unless the vehicle should not be used now.

idle.what: The vehicle stood still for a long time with the engine running.
idle.action: Idling wastes fuel. Ask the driver to switch off the engine while waiting.

parking.what: The vehicle has been parked longer than expected.
parking.action: Check whether the vehicle is waiting for work or has a problem.

fuelTheft.what: The fuel level dropped suddenly — fuel may have been taken.
fuelTheft.action: Check the place and time of the drop and talk to the driver.

fuelLow.what: The fuel tank is nearly empty.
fuelLow.action: Ask the driver to refuel soon.

temperature.what: The temperature sensor reading is outside the allowed range.
temperature.action: If the vehicle carries temperature-sensitive cargo, contact the driver now.

sleep.what: The tracker switched to (or woke from) power-saving mode because the vehicle is parked.
sleep.action: This is normal — no action needed.

reboot.action: One restart is normal. If it restarts often, check its power supply.

motion.what: The vehicle started moving or came to a stop.
motion.action: No action needed — this is a status update.

maintenance.what: The vehicle is due for service.
maintenance.action: Book the service so the vehicle does not break down.

trip.what: A trip started, ended, or took longer than planned.
trip.action: Open the trip to see the route and times.

routine.what: A routine location report from the tracker.

generic.what: The tracker reported an event for this vehicle.
generic.action: Open the details and the map to see what happened around this time.

operations.title: Mine operations
operations.subtitle: When each machine started sending data, how far it travelled, and how many pit-to-dump services it completed.
operations.activityHint: Start of work is the first stored position after the device was assigned to this organisation. Distance ignores jumps faster than 100 km/h. Offline time is the gap beyond five minutes between fixes, including the tail to the end of the range. A device that never sent a fix is marked silent.
operations.haulHint: A service is counted when a truck on this route enters the origin, leaves it, and enters the destination. Time in the origin is loading. Distance and hours are the loaded leg. The shovel inside the origin during loading is credited with that load. The work day starts at the first shift's start hour and shifts run back to back; a service belongs to the shift in which loading started.
operations.membersHint: Trucks complete the haul. Shovels stay in the origin and are credited for each load.

operations.presetHint: Ranges follow the work day (from the first shift's start) so a night shift is never split.
